newsitem.title: FINLAND: White House condemns Tel Aviv bombing.
newsitem.headline: White House condemns Tel Aviv bombing.

text.p: A senior White House official on Friday condemned the bombing of a Tel Aviv cafe that killed at least four people and said President Bill Clinton would also speak out against the attack.

"We're all saddened to learn of this explosion in Tel Aviv," the official said. "We all know that the way to make progress is not through violence, but through working together and our thoughts are now with the victims of this terrible act and their families."
The official, who asked not to be identified, said Clinton, who was in Helsinki for a two-day summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin, would be "speaking on our behalf on this".
"We condemn this act of violence as we're sure all friends of peace will," the official said.

In Tel Aviv, army radio said Israeli police believed a suicide bomber had carried out the attack at a cafe that killed at least four people and wounded dozens. The radio said it was not clear whether the bomber was among the four dead.

Asked if the United States believed a controversial Israeli decision to break ground for a housing development in an Arab neighbourhood in East Jerusalem had contributed to the attack, the official said: "This is an act of terror. This is not an act of politics."
